messages:
hannah: Quick follow-up to the pin/rollout metadata RFC. Proposal: a compact "pin envelope" that is small in the hot index (<= 80 bytes) but references a full, auditable manifest in object store. The envelope is the canonical thing resolvers use; manifest is for humans/audit. Thoughts?

joel: Nice. What do you encode in the envelope vs leave in the manifest? Trying to balance expressivity vs hot-path size.

hannah: Minimal for serve-time: model_hash (20B), epoch (varint), rollout_tag (small int), fallback_ptr (varint), expiry_ts (optional), flags byte. Plus a small provenance: key_id (2B) + sig (8B truncated HMAC). Envelope prefix includes version e.g., PENv1.

maya: From runtime: if we can verify envelope sig and unpack those fields we avoid manifest fetches for 99% requests. For diagnostics we expand async. Good win for latency.

frank: How do we handle complex rollouts (weights, canaries)? If envelope only has rollout_tag, resolver must consult separate routing-svc keyed by rollout_tag. Is that ok?

joel: I think separating routing policy is preferable. It allows retargeting without repinning. So rollout_tag -> routing policy table (in-memory). Envelope becomes small stable pointer.

hannah: Exactly. Also include a short provenance_hint string (enum) so the resolver knows whether to rely on token verification only or to fetch manifest for additional policies.

ops-kate: Ops note: our hot index stores millions of tenant entries. If we replace bulky JSON manifest with 64-80B envelope, memory drops a lot. Migration?

hannah: Migration plan: additive index value: {"envelope":"PENv1...","manifest_url":"s3://...","manifest_hash":"sha256:..."}. New resolvers prefer envelope; legacy clients read manifest_url. We'll dual-write for 3 weeks in flight.

frank: Signature truncation: 8B truncated HMAC yields collision risk. We rotate keys and monitor false acceptance. Also maintain a short hot denylist for immediate revocation.

joel: For key distribution, resolvers cache verification keys from control-plane/KMS for ~60s. Control-plane rotates keys with staged rollout; resolvers fall back to manifest on verification failures.

maya: Observability: emit metrics: envelope.verify_fail_rate, envelope.fallback_to_manifest_rate, envelope.expiry_reject_rate, envelope.age_ms distribution. Also log a short expand_id in traces when manifest is fetched so Console can link to expanded info.

hannah: Envelope format sketch (pseudo):

PENv1.<base64(payload)>.<sig>

payload (binary-packed): tenant_varint | model_hash(20B) | epoch_varint | rollout_tag_varint | fallback_varint | expiry(4B opt) | flags(1B) | key_id(2B)

sig = HMAC-SHA256(k, payload) truncated to 8B. Expected total ~ 56-80 bytes depending on varints.

ops-kate: Nice. For emergency retirements we need immediate global invalidation. Per-request denylist is expensive. Instead: publish small push-based revoke set to resolvers that is kept in-memory (hot) and apply before trusting envelope. Blacklist size will be tiny in practice.

frank: Another edge: staged rollbacks where you want to revert only a subset of tenants. We can publish tenant-scoped deny messages via the same push channel, resolvers check in-memory set keyed by tenant_id or token hash. Cheap for hot hits.

joel: Console UX: show envelope expansion on hover; Console calls expand API which fetches manifest_url and returns readable JSON. We must ensure expand API is rate-limited and paged for big manifests.

maya: Testing: add canary path where 1% of resolvers run in manifest-first mode and emit diff telemetry. Gate on envelope.fallback_rate < 0.2% and verify no p99 regressions.

hannah: Migration checklist draft:
- Control-plane dual-write index values for 3w
- Deploy resolver change in canary cluster (manifest-fallback OK)
- Monitor envelope.verify_fail_rate, fallback_rate, p99 latency
- If metrics pass, flip default to envelope-first
- Keep manifests in object store indefinitely for audits

ops-kate: Ops will add playbook steps for key rotation, revoke push, and emergency rollback. Also weekly snapshot job to inline large manifests for tenants doing aggressive churn.

frank: One more thought: to help debugging, include a short human-readable hint (2-3 char enum) in envelope decoded payload that Console can display without fetching manifest (e.g., "ST" for stable, "CN" for canary, "RT" for retired).

joel: +1. That will help SREs triage quickly.

audit-bot: snapshot created: control-plane/designs/pin-envelope/6100000000

hannah: Action items:
- @joel: resolver PR to parse PENv1 and verify sig (ETA 1w)
- @maya: instrumentation + expand API (ETA 1w)
- @ops-kate: migration playbook + revoke push spec (ETA 4d)
- @frank: security note on truncated HMAC risks & mitigations (ETA 3d)

hannah: Thanks all, we'll review progress in the architecture sync next Tuesday. :thumbsup:
